To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The majority of customers participate in their banking relationship.

(1) the benefits which accrue to banks from developing relationships are not as high as they might be because customers are unwilling to participate in the relationship, and (2) customers are unwilling to engage in relationship building because the benefits they perceive from doing so are not high enough to compensate them for the costs of doing so.
* Customers who participate in the banking relationship are more satisfied with their bank than those who do not.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the extent and nature of participation in the banking customer relationship, and its implications for the quality of service.
the benefits which accrue to customers from their participation in the production of services.
the extent to which customers are willing to participate in the production and delivery of a service and the benefits which accrue from such participation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the majority of customers in the UK small business sector participate in the banking relationship and that this participation is beneficial.
the benefits of participating are greater than the costs.
participation in a banking relationship is a positive and worthwhile activity for small firms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the majority of small business customers are not willing to participate in their relationship with the bank.
the benefits which accrue from participation in the banking relationships are not sufficient to outweigh the disadvantages.
customers do perceive benefits from participating in the banking relationships, but that the benefits are not sufficient to ensure that all customers participate in the relationship.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the benefits of participating are not evenly spread across all customers, with the most loyal customers being the least likely to participate.
customers are not passive recipients of service.
customers are more likely to participate in the banking relationship where they perceive that their bank provides high quality service.
